Here is a structured 12-week program tailored for a 47-year-old female client, advanced lifter, early perimenopause with irregular cycles (23–52 days), experiencing vasomotor symptoms (hot flashes, heat intolerance). GP cleared for resistance training with bone density considerations. Restrictions: no sauna, no fasted HIIT in heat, structured cooling required. Begin 2026-06-01. The plan emphasizes resistance training with hormonal/thermal considerations, periodization, built-in cooling strategies, and nutrition/recovery guidance.

Overview and goals
- Primary goals: maintain and progress lean mass and strength, protect bone health, manage vasomotor symptoms with training and cooling strategies, optimize energy and mood, and support overall health during perimenopause.
- Training frequency: 4 days/week resistance training + 1 optional light conditioning or mobility day. Include 1–2 deload weeks.
- Temperature management: sessions scheduled in cooler parts of the day or in air-conditioned space; utilize pre/post-cool-down, hydration, electrolytes, and cooling methods (cool towels, fans, cold drink, cooling vest if available).
- Nutrition: adequate total calories with emphasis on protein intake (~1.6–2.0 g/kg/day), balanced carbs around training, hydration with electrolytes, and strategic intake of phytoestrogens and calcium/vitamin D as indicated by bone health status. Consider small meals to maintain energy and minimize vasomotor symptom triggers (spicy foods, caffeine timing).
- Recovery: emphasis on sleep quality, stress management, and active recovery. Include mobility and mobility-focused sessions to support joints and posture.

Key structure
- Phases: 4 phases x 3 weeks each, with a deload/transition week every 4th week (Weeks 4, 8, 12 as appropriate) or a lighter week within each phase. For clarity, Week 1–3, Week 4 (deload), Week 5–7, Week 8 (deload), Week 9–11, Week 12 (deload or peak-lite).
- Weekly layout: 4 training days (A, B, C, D) with push, pull, legs, accessory/technique or upper-lower split depending on client preference. Include 1 optional light conditioning day.

12-week plan (start date: 2026-06-01)

Phase 1: Foundations and adaptation (Weeks 1–3)
Objectives: establish movement quality, reintroduce higher-volume work safely, build base strength, establish cooling protocols.

Week 1 (2026-06-01 to 2026-06-07)
- Day A — Lower body strength
  - Back squat: 4 sets x 5 reps at 75% 1RM
  - Romanian deadlift: 3x6 at moderate load
  - Bulgarian split squats: 3x8 per leg
  - Glute bridge or hip thrust: 3x8
  - calf raises: 3x12
  - core: pallof press 3x10 each side
- Day B — Push
  - Barbell bench press: 4x6 at 70–75%
  - Overhead press (standing): 3x8
  - Dumbbell incline: 3x10
  - Triceps pushdown: 3x12
  - Lateral raises: 3x12
- Day C — Pull
  - Bent-over barbell row: 4x6
  - Weighted pull-ups or lat pulldown: 3x8
  - seated cable row: 3x10
  - Face pulls: 3x15
  - Biceps curl: 3x12
- Day D — Mobility/Conditioning with cooling
  - Mobility flow: 15–20 min (hips, thoracic spine, shoulders)
  - Light conditioning: 20–25 min easy steady-state on bike/elliptical at RPE 4–5
  - Post-session: cold towel 5–10 min, hydration, electrolyte balance

Week 2
- Increase intensity modestly (add ~2–5% to main lifts) while preserving form
- Keep sets: 4x5 for main lifts; accessory volumes stay similar
- Maintain cooling strategies: pre-cool if hot, maintain hydration

Week 3
- Similar structure, aim to complete most sets with good technique; monitor vasomotor symptoms
- Add one tempo set for squats or deadlifts (2-second eccentric)

Week 4 — Deload week
- Reduce volume by ~40–50% and keep loads light (about 50–60% of Week 3)
- Focus on technique, mobility, and recovery
- Keep cooling protocols and hydration; consider brisk walks or light cycling for 20–30 minutes if tolerated

Phase 2: Strength gain with endurance work (Weeks 5–7)
Objectives: build strength with controlled volume, introduce more structured conditioning while maintaining cooling strategies.

Week 5
- Day A — Lower body strength
  - Back squat: 5x4 at 80% 1RM
  - RDL or stiff-leg deadlift: 3x6
  - Bulgarian split squat: 3x6–8
  - Hip thrust: 3x8
  - Calf raises: 3x12
- Day B — Push
  - Bench press: 4x5 at 75–80%
  - Overhead press: 3x6
  - Dumbbell flyes or push-ups: 3x10
  - Triceps extension: 3x12
  - Lateral raises: 3x12
- Day C — Pull
  - Barbell row: 4x5
  - Lat pulldown: 3x8
  - Dumbbell rows: 3x8 per side
  - Face pulls: 3x15
  - Biceps: hammer curl 3x12
- Day D — Conditioning + cooling
  - 20–30 min interval work but at moderate heat? Given restriction “no fasted HIIT in heat,” schedule this in a cooler context: 1) steady-state cardio 25–35 min or 2) low-intensity intervals in cool environment (e.g., 6x1 min effort at RPE 6 with 2 min easy, in air-conditioned space)
  - Post-workout cooling: cold towel, fan, hydration

Week 6
- Reps: 4–5 sets for main lifts, main lifts at around 78–82% 1RM
- Add tempo or paused reps on one main lift per session to improve technique
- Keep accessory volume similar

Week 7
- Slight progression; introduce density blocks: 3 rounds of main lift complex with short rest
- Maintain cooling strategies and hydration

Week 8 — Deload week
- Reduce volume by ~40–50% and loads to 50–60%
- Focus on mobility, sleep quality, nutrition timing around workouts

Phase 3: Hypertrophy and muscular balance with stability (Weeks 9–11)
Objectives: emphasize hypertrophy and muscle balance with attention to bone health and perimenopause symptoms.

Week 9
- Day A — Lower
  - Front squat or back squat: 4x6 at 70–75%
  - Romanian deadlift: 3x6–8
  - Lunges: 3x8 per leg
  - Glute ham raises or Nordic ham curls: 3x6

  - Triceps pushdown or skull crushers: 3x12
  - Lateral raises: 3x12
- Day C — Pull
  - T-bar row or barbell row: 4x8
  - Pull-ups or lat pulldown: 3x8–10
  - Inverted rows or machine rows: 3x10
  - Face pulls: 3x15
  - Biceps: cable curl 3x12
- Day D — Active recovery/conditioning with cooling
  - 20–30 min easy cardio in cool environment (RPE 4–5)
  - Mobility flow and breathing work for vasomotor symptom management

Week 10
- Increase volume slightly on accessory work; keep main lifts within 4–5 sets
- Introduce supersets on upper body days sparingly, ensuring form, no overheating

Week 11
- Push for slight PRs in non-peak fashion; maintain form and tolerability
- Emphasize scapular stability work and thoracic mobility

Week 12 — Deload or peak-lite
- Deload: reduce overall volume and keep intensity moderate
- If you want a performance benchmark, test 1RM for one lower body lift and one press with warm-up, ensuring full cooling and symptom control

Phase 4: Consolidation and program cycle end (Optional deload if continuing)
If continuing, you can repeat a similar structure but with progressive overload adjustments and new exercise variations to prevent plateaus. Include 1–2 microcycles of higher intensity for strength while respecting symptom management.

Daily session structure and considerations
- Warm-up: 8–12 minutes general (bike, row) + 5–8 minutes mobility focusing on spine, hips, shoulders.
- Main lifts: 4 sets of 4–6 reps (or 4–5 sets of 5) depending on phase; work within RPE 7–8 for main lifts, ensuring technique.
- Accessory work: 3–4 sets of 8–12 reps; focus on muscle groups targeted to balance strength and aesthetic goals while reducing joint stress.
- Tempo: emphasize controlled eccentric (2–3 seconds) with solid concentric; vary tempo at times for hypertrophy.
- Rest intervals: 2–3 minutes between heavy sets; 60–90 seconds for accessories.
- Cooling and thermoregulation: use cold towels pre/post; ice pack or cooling vest if available; keep a fan nearby; ensure the training space remains cool (air-conditioned preferred). Hydration every 15–20 minutes during workouts; have electrolytes on hot days.

  - Monday: Day A Lower
  - Tuesday: Day B Push
  - Thursday: Day C Pull
  - Friday: Day D Conditioning/Mobility
  - Optional Saturday: Light technique work or mobility (15–20 minutes)

Nutrition guidance
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day distributed across 3–5 meals; include 0.4–0.6 g/kg per feeding when possible, particularly post-workout.
- Calories: aimed at maintenance or slight surplus to support strength gains, adjusting for cycle phase if cycles influence appetite; perimenopause symptoms may affect energy, so plan energy around training days.
- Carbohydrates: around training windows; moderate to high around workouts to support performance and recovery.
- Fats: include healthy fats; ensure omega-3 intake to support inflammation and overall health.
- Calcium and vitamin D: ensure adequate intake per bone health guidelines; consider supplementation if dietary intake is low or if vitamin D is deficient.
- Hydration: maintain baseline hydration, increase around training; monitor symptoms and heat exposure.
- Symptom management via nutrition: spicy foods and caffeine can trigger vasomotor symptoms in some; consider caffeine timing and spicy foods timing around workouts to minimize symptoms.
- Iron: monitor if symptomatic (anemia risk); ensure iron intake from foods; consider iron supplementation only if advised by clinician.

Recovery and lifestyle
- Sleep: 7–9 hours nightly; prioritize consistent sleep schedule; use cooling strategies to improve sleep quality if hot at night.
- Stress management: breathing routines, mindfulness; journaling to help with symptom tracking.
- Mobility and posture: 10–15 minutes daily focusing on thoracic spine, hips, and shoulders.
- Thermoregulation: avoid overheating pre-workout; use cooling methods before sessions; ensure comfortable ambient temperature during sessions.
- Communication with client and GP: track symptoms, cycle irregularities, and response to training; adjust schedule around cycle as needed if symptoms are more pronounced during certain days; confirm that perimenopause management considerations are ongoing.

Tracking and progression
- Track 1RM for a main lift (e.g., squat or bench) at the start and after Week 6 and Week 12 if appropriate, using safe testing and cooling strategies.
- Use a weekly rating of perceived exertion (RPE) for main sets to adjust loads.
- Track vasomotor symptoms daily (hot flashes frequency/severity) and correlate with training sessions and environmental factors to refine session timing and cooling strategies.

Notes for the trainer
- Given perimenopause and heat intolerance, prioritize cooler environments, avoid aggressive heat exposure, and ensure a structured cooling protocol is in place.
- If symptoms worsen on certain days (e.g., around late luteal phase if cycle becomes more regular in future), plan lighter sessions or switch to non-peak intensity days.
- If bone density concerns, avoid high-impact jumps or plyometrics that may be too jarring; however, maintain bone-loading resistance exercises with proper progression and technique.

- Phase structure: 4 phases of 3 weeks each, with a deload/transition week at the end of Phase 1 (Week 4), Phase 2 deload (Week 8), and Phase 3 deload/peak-lite (Week 12). The plan is organized as weekly blocks with explicit sessions, sets, reps, and progression cues.
- Training split: 4 days/week resistance training (A, B, C, D) plus an optional light cardio/conditioning day and a separate cardio integration plan (kept within heat/cooling constraints).
- Phase 2 push-intensity upgrade (Weeks 5–7) to drive bench/overhead pressing strength with higher intensity.
- Hot yoga incorporated: 2 sessions/week with careful scheduling to minimize heat/overload impact.
- Cardio framework: maintained aerobic base with heat-aware, cooler-environment cardio 2–3 days/week (non-fasted), plus optional post-lift cardio and NEAT emphasis. Fat-loss cardio discussions provided previously are retained as options if fat loss is a goal, but with emphasis on safety and recovery.
- Nutrition plan and bone-health focus: macro targets, protein emphasis (1.6–2.0 g/kg/day), calcium/vitamin D, magnesium, vitamin K2, omega-3s, and hydration/electrolytes. Nutrition details adjusted around workouts and cooling considerations.
- 1RM testing: guidance provided for end of Phase 3 (Weeks 9–11) with safety considerations; submaximal testing alternatives provided if needed.
- We’ve kept the plan adaptable to equipment, climate, and exact 1RM values.

Important: To tailor the exact weekly weights, volumes, and progression to absolute numbers (kg or lbs) and to match your client’s current 1RM(s), please share:
- Current or most recent 1RM for squat (back or front), bench press, and overhead press.
- Body weight (or target weight) and approximate training age or recent performance data.
- Any equipment constraints (barbell availability, dumbbells range, machines).
- Any dietary preferences/restrictions that would affect nutrition plan specifics.

12-Week Plan: Start date 2026-06-01

Phase 1: Foundations and adaptation (Weeks 1–3)
Objectives: movement quality, establish safe higher-volume work, reintroduce resistance with controlled progression, build base tolerance to cooling protocols, set hydration/electrolyte routines.

Weekly layout
- 4 main training days: A (Lower), B (Push), C (Pull), D (Mobility/Conditioning with cooling)
- 1 optional light cardio/NEAT day (non-consecutive)
- Hot yoga: begin Week 2 at 1x/week; Week 3 add 1 more if well-tolerated
- Cardio: 2–3 days/week integrated, in cool environments; 20–40 minutes total per session per guidance below

Phase 1 specifics

Week 1 (2026-06-01 to 2026-06-07)
- Day A — Lower
  - Back squat: 4x5 at 75% 1RM
  - Romanian deadlift: 3x6
  - Bulgarian split squat: 3x8 per leg
  - Hip thrust: 3x8
  - Calf raises: 3x12
  - Core: Pallof press 3x10 each side
- Day B — Push
  - Barbell bench press: 4x6 at 70–75%
  - Overhead press: 3x8
  - Dumbbell incline: 3x10
  - Triceps pushdown: 3x12
  - Lateral raises: 3x12
- Day C — Pull
  - Bent-over barbell row: 4x6
  - Lat pulldown or weighted pull-ups: 3x8
  - Seated cable row: 3x10
  - Face pulls: 3x15
  - Biceps curl: 3x12
- Day D — Mobility/Conditioning + cooling
  - Mobility flow 15–20 min
  - Conditioning: 20–25 min zone 2 cardio (RPE 4–5)
  - Post: cold towel 5–10 min, hydration/electrolytes
- Optional: 1 light cardio day (20–30 min) on off days; prioritize thermoregulation

Week 2
- Increase main lifts by ~2–5% if technique/feel allows; keep volume consistent
- Maintain Day D cooling protocol; add 1 tempo set to squat or deadlift (2-second eccentric)

Week 3
- Similar structure; introduce one tempo set for a main lift (e.g., squat or bench) to promote technique and time under tension
- Add one 6–8 min mobility/breathing block post-session if needed
- Cardio: maintain 20–35 min depending on energy; introduce 1 light interval (4 × 1 min at RPE 6 with 2 min easy) if tolerable and environment controlled

Week 4 — Deload week
- Reduce volume by 40–50%; loads 50–60% of Week 3
- Focus on technique, mobility, sleep, and recovery
- Cardio: 2 sessions, 20–25 minutes at RPE 4–5; optional light intervals if energy allows
- Hot yoga: pause or reduce to 1x/wk if needed due to fatigue

Phase 2: Strength gain with endurance work (Weeks 5–7)
Objectives: heavier push strength, controlled progression, maintain aerobic base, add timed conditioning while preserving cooling.

  - Dumbbell row: 3x8 per side
  - Face pulls: 3x15
  - Biceps: hammer curl 3x12
- Day D — Conditioning + cooling
  - 20–30 min cardio in cool environment (RPE 4–5)
- Hot yoga: 1x/week (Week 5) scheduled on a lighter day or after a mobility session; ensure adequate cooling

  - 1–2 light 1RM attempts for squat and bench (or a 3–5RM alternative if needed) with ample warm-up and cooling
  - Post-test deload protocol if needed
